essence: The book of knowledge closes by proving its knowers are one: no shared world-path without one light, and the light itself admits no difference.
Every rival witness is conscripted rather than refuted — Sāṃkhya, Mīmāṃsā, Vaiśeṣika all point, unwittingly, at the same self-luminous one.
Objections about difference, error and mutual expectation are settled inside the unity: māyā arranges the many without ever leaving the one.
Lordship turns out to need no addition: fixed self-awareness just is the great Lord, closing the adhikāra where it began — with the one.
